title: Division with try-catch
description: Create a method that receives two integers and shows the result of the division. Use try-catch to catch ArithmeticException when dividing by zero, showing 'Error: Cannot divide by zero'. Use finally to always show 'Operation completed'.
hints: Wrap the division operation in a try block
In the catch, capture ArithmeticException and show the error message
The finally block always runs; put 'Operation completed' there
solutionExplanation: The try block executes the division. If the divisor is 0, ArithmeticException is thrown and caught in the catch block. The finally block always runs, whether the exception occurred or not, guaranteeing that 'Operation completed' is shown in both cases.
expectedOutput:
Result: 5
Operation completed
---
Error: Cannot divide by zero
Operation completed

title: Safe reading
description: Create a method called leerArchivo that receives a String with the path of a file. Use try-catch to attempt to read the file. If it fails, show a friendly message: 'Could not read file: {ruta}'. Always show 'Reading finished' in a finally block.
hints: Use Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(ruta)) to read the file inside a try block
Catch IOException in the catch block and show the message with the file path
Put 'Reading finished' in the finally block so it is always shown
solutionExplanation: The method uses Files.readAllBytes to attempt to read the whole file. If the file does not exist or there is an I/O error, IOException is caught and a friendly message with the path is shown. The finally block always runs, showing 'Reading finished' regardless of the result.
expectedOutput:
Could not read file: datos.txt
Reading finished
---
Could not read file: inexistente.txt
Reading finished

title: Connection manager
description: Create a Conexion class implementing AutoCloseable with a name. Its close() method must show 'Closing connection: {nombre}'. Then create a method that uses try-with-resources to open two connections (one valid and one that throws IOException). Observe how the connections close automatically in reverse order.
hints: An AutoCloseable class must have a close() method that may throw Exception
In the constructor, show 'Opening connection: {nombre}' when creating the instance
try-with-resources automatically closes the resources in reverse order of opening
Make abrirConexion throw IOException if the name contains 'Respaldo' to simulate a failure
solutionExplanation: The Conexion class implements AutoCloseable to be used in try-with-resources. Its constructor shows a message when opening and close() when closing. The abrirConexion method throws IOException if the name contains 'Respaldo'. In the try-with-resources, the first connection (BD-Principal) opens correctly, but the second one throws an exception. Java automatically closes BD-Principal in reverse order before handling the exception. If both opened successfully, both would be closed at the end of the block.
expectedOutput:
Opening connection: BD-Principal
Closing connection: BD-Principal
Error: Could not connect to: BD-Respaldo
